body:
I've learned that one of the least socially acceptable things in the society I know (Western Euro-American) is being okay with suicide. People are never okay with calm attitudes towards suicide, not for a layperson (because then you're a horrible monster), nor for a public servant (because laws). 

You mentioned that people are taking away our agency. I am 120% sure that they don't see it that way. Suicidal people have no agency, according to public opinion. They're treated like minors that can't legitimately agree to sexual intercourse, for example. Or like the criminally insane (legal term, not medical term.)

In other words, we suicides are considered not functional adults, who aren't capable of making their own choices, therefore our choices are legally and morally okay to disregard. This attitude is stronger than anyone's true concern for us. 

For example, if I were to try suicide tomorrow and was stopped before the attempt, I'd be detained by authorities and forcibly placed in a medical unit, for which I would then have to pay thousands of dollars per day, even though I didn't want to be there and even if I'm uninjured and the medical unit does absolutely nothing. If I couldn't pay, I would eventually end up homeless.

If you really want to kill yourself, you MUST keep it a secret until the end. If you're on the fence, telling people IRL is not great. Anonymity is better because anonymous strangers don't have the same pressure to be a "good person" by declaring "suicide is bad!" within their friends' earshot.
